question: By whose agency does the speaker claim to have come to know the determination of the Kaula doctrine?
premises: The speaker addresses the lord of the Kaulas.
The speaker claims to have become known or to have come to know something.
That knowledge is identified as the determination of the Kaula doctrine.
The means cited is the grace of the one addressed.
inference: By the grace of the lord of the Kaulas, the speaker has come to know the determination of the Kaula doctrine.
uncertainties: The precise sense of jñāta in this construction remains open to interpretation.
plain_english: By your grace, O lord of the Kaulas, I have come to know the determination of the Kaula doctrine.
